title: Attempts log path is written without any repository or path safety checks

finding.claim: Attempts log path is written without any repository or path safety checks
finding.evidence: The code opens a user-supplied path directly for append, so invoking the CLI with a crafted '--attempts-log' can write arbitrary files accessible to the process rather than being constrained to the repo or output directory.
finding.recommendation: Validate '--attempts-log' before opening it. At minimum, resolve it against an allowed base directory and reject paths outside that base, or document and intentionally gate arbitrary file writes behind a separate explicit option.

probe.summary: `probes/gap_attempts_log_probe.py`, result `gap-attempts-log-bca4074a632c.txt`: - **P5 provenance — condition holds.** Every `attempts_log` reference in the source tree: one argparse definition (`--attempts-log`, cli.py:1706) and the reads of `args.attempts_log` in the review path. No environment variable, no user/project config file, no policy file, and nothing read from the repository under review can set it. The only principal who can supply the path is the operator running the CLI, typed on their own command line. - **Mechanism — real, as claimed.** A functional CLI run (agent stub seat, temp cwd) with `--attempts-log` pointing outside any repository wrote the entry there: exit 0, one JSON line, append mode. The entry is the run's own telemetry (gate, seat statuses, patch hash — no diff text, no secrets). There is no containment check at HEAD, and none is bypassed: the write goes where the operator pointed it, the same trust class as `--out`. So both sides are partly right: the claim's mechanism is accurately described; its security framing needs an attacker, and the only person who can aim this flag is the person who owns the files it can reach.
